01 — WHY WE DO THIS

Opportunity should not decide who gets to understand.

We have benefited from academic experience, supportive schools, and people willing to share what they know. OpenBridge is our way of passing that support forward.

We believe knowledge grows when it is shared. By offering our time and subject experience, we hope to help students with fewer educational opportunities build confidence, ask questions freely, and discover what they can do.

We are student tutors—not qualified adult teachers. That means we teach honestly, stay within what we know, prepare carefully, and ask for adult guidance when needed.

Subjects are grouped around skills that work together, so each session has a clear focus rather than feeling like a random list of topics.

Digital Creation

Learn to think like a builder: break down problems, test ideas, and create projects using accessible technology.

DIGITAL CREATION

Make ideas work.

We introduce coding through Scratch, then use projects, puzzles, and debugging to develop logical thinking. Learners also build practical confidence with digital tools, online safety, and responsible technology use.

  • Designing interactive Scratch projects
  • Loops, conditions, variables, and debugging
  • Safe, confident use of everyday technology
  • Breaking large problems into clear steps

How it works

Simple from first question to first session.

OpenBridge is preparing to launch. This is the process we plan to use; final availability and scheduling will be confirmed with each family.

  1. 1

    Tell us what support is needed

    A parent, guardian, school, or learner registers interest and shares the subject, age range, and goal.

  2. 2

    We check the fit

    We match the topic to a tutor and say clearly if it is outside our experience or availability.

  3. 3

    Agree a safe time

    Session details are arranged through the approved parent, guardian, or school contact.

  4. 4

    Meet and learn online

    The learner joins a free, focused video session—planned through Google Meet—with clear goals and next steps.

✓

Trust & transparency

Student-led should also mean carefully led.

Before bookings open, OpenBridge will publish a clear safeguarding process. These are the standards we are building around:

01

Adults stay informed

Scheduling and key communication for younger learners will include a parent, guardian, or responsible school contact.

02

Clear online boundaries

No private social-media contact, no unnecessary personal information, and no recording without explicit agreement.

03

Honest tutor limits

We will never claim adult teaching qualifications. If a topic is beyond us, we will say so.

04

Learning, not childcare

Sessions are focused academic support. They do not replace school, professional teaching, or adult supervision.

Launch status: Interest stage. Final booking, consent, supervision, and reporting procedures are still being confirmed.

Questions

Good to know.

Is tutoring really free?+

Yes. OpenBridge is being created as a free tutoring initiative. We do not plan to charge learners or families for sessions.

Are you qualified teachers?+

No. We are student tutors sharing subjects we know well. We will be transparent about our experience, stay within our limits, and direct learners to a teacher or specialist when appropriate.

What ages can take part?+

We are primarily designing sessions for learners around ages 8–14+. The best fit will still depend on the subject, learner’s needs, safeguarding arrangements, and tutor availability.

Where will sessions happen?+

Sessions are planned to be online, likely through Google Meet. The confirmed platform and joining details will be shared through the approved adult contact.

Can you help with every topic listed?+

Not automatically. The list shows our subject areas, but we will check every request first. If a specific topic is beyond our current experience, we will be honest rather than guess.

How do we sign up?+

Use the registration form below. When you submit it, your email app will open with the registration details ready to send to FFA OpenBridge.

Technology & science

Kenta

About me

Hey! I’m Kenta, an IGCSE student with a strong interest in technology, science, coding, and problem-solving. I enjoy exploring how things work and turning ideas into useful, creative projects. That curiosity shapes the way I learn and the way I help others.

Learning by building

I’ve worked on several independent software projects, including music and technology applications. Building these projects has given me hands-on experience with programming, debugging, and creative problem-solving. It has also taught me to break a larger challenge into smaller steps, test different approaches, and learn from mistakes along the way.

Leadership & teamwork

At school, I’m involved in technical production and leadership, helping guide and train younger students in using technology and working as a team. I enjoy explaining unfamiliar tools clearly, listening to questions, and helping others feel more confident as they practise.

How I teach

At OpenBridge, I teach Scratch coding, technology literacy, critical thinking, and general science. My approach is practical and interactive: break complicated ideas into clear steps, explore examples, and give learners opportunities to try things themselves. I want students to understand not only the answer, but why it works—and to enjoy the process of figuring it out.

Mathematics & science

Gao

About my subjects

I support learners across mathematics and science, from core foundations through to harder, more advanced topics. My OpenBridge subject areas include core, general, and advanced mathematics, as well as biology, physics, and general science.

Humanities, science & debate

Cooper

About me

Hi, I’m Cooper. My academic interests are centred on the humanities, particularly Global Perspectives, Environmental Management, History, and Geography. I also enjoy science, especially physics. I like connecting ideas across subjects, asking questions, and using evidence to understand different perspectives.

Academic background

In Year 9, I achieved an A* in Global Perspectives and A grades in History, Geography, and science. These are Year 9 grades, rather than IGCSE results. Alongside these subjects, Environmental Management is another area of particular interest to me.

Debate & Model United Nations

I’ve trained in debate for three years and taken part in around ten debate and Model United Nations competitions combined. My goal is to earn a place in Thailand’s National Debate Team Pool. My debate achievements include Junior Champions at Power of Persuasion 2025, 2nd Best Novice Speaker, 6th U15 Best Speaker, and a semi-final finish at Anglo Blend. Across five MUN conferences, I’ve received two Best Delegate awards and one honourable mention.

How I teach

Debate and MUN have helped me develop research, public speaking, teamwork, critical thinking, and the ability to build well-supported arguments. At OpenBridge, I hope to use those skills to explain ideas clearly and make unfamiliar concepts easier to understand. I want learners to feel comfortable asking questions, sharing their perspectives, and building confidence in how they think and communicate.
